\section{Validated rational bounds}\label{sec:certificate}

The accompanying exact-rational computation instantiates the identity chart
at
\[
 t_0=\frac15,\qquad \rho=1,\qquad M=8,
\]
and the transition/cut overlap at $\delta=1/5$.  Machin's identity encloses
$\pi$; alternating or positive Taylor series and compact exponential
majorants bound elementary functions; rational square-root intervals are
checked by squaring their endpoints.  Every theorem-critical comparison is
an integer comparison.  Binary floating point is used only in the separate
formula diagnostic.

The identity-chart positivity floor is greater than
$1-3.0\times10^{-18}$.  On the larger interval
$0\le\theta\le\pi-1/5$, the time-maximized transition bound gives
\[
 \widehat Q_0<0.985,\qquad 1-\widehat Q_0>0.0159.
\]
The exact cut-pair condition has positive margin
$\pi^2-t_0-\pi\delta>9.03$.  Thus every denominator used in the global
three-chart theorem has a recorded positive lower bound.  The transition
derivative constants are intentionally conservative; all orders zero through
eight, together with the transition-chart geometric constants, are included
in the machine-readable record.

The normalized tail upper bounds at $\rho=1$ are $0.595$, $0.0913$, and
$0.00376$ for $t=1/5,1/10,1/20$.  The validated plaquette margins are
\[
 \lambda_{\rm rad}>4.545,\qquad
 \lambda_{\rm tan}>2.755,\qquad
 tR_2<0.091,\quad tR_3<0.058,\quad tR_4<0.101.
\]

The checker recomputes the file digest, rational ordering, both positivity
floors, every Bell-polynomial logarithmic bound, the cut-pair margin, the
plaquette bounds, and all geometric-tail contractions.  The digest checks
byte-level integrity only; it is not treated as a mathematical argument.
A separate numerical diagnostic compares \eqref{eq:character} and
\eqref{eq:image} on 21 cells, including both removable endpoints.  Its
maximum relative-or-absolute discrepancy is $1.91\times10^{-15}$.  This
diagnostic detects convention or implementation errors but is not used to
prove an inequality.
